runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: Consistent Brighton 6f form (six runs on good) but has won nothing in 15 similar-going starts; natural hold-up operator who will be shuffled further back than ideal in this compressed field, limiting her scope off this uncontested pace.

runners_data.name: Battle Point
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old without a place in eight similar-going starts across his last 15; Jim Attwater runner who will want to come from off the pace but has no realistic closing position in a steady-run race, and the form string reads poorly.

runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed front-runner and the pivotal horse tactically; Kieren Fox should lead unchallenged and the stable (Attwater, 1W from last 13) has a recent course second to back it up — 1W2P in similar going is the standout strike-rate in this field.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with blinkers, whose most recent Brighton run ended twelfth of twelve; natural hold-up horse compressed further rearward by field congestion, and his sim-going record of 0W1P from only four runs suggests limited upside.

runners_data.name: Lynwood Lad
runners_data.note: Has run prominently in the past (hood worn, hg:p tag) and is one of the redistribution horses most capable of pushing forward to secure a better berth; Gary & Josh Moore yard in fair form (4/31 last 14), and his one win in similar going keeps him relevant if he gets cover in a stalking spot.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Chute
runners_data.note: Stepping up from five furlongs having finished no closer than seventh in his last five; 54 days off the track is a notable absence and his sim-going record (0W1P in five) gives little encouragement for a hold-up horse needing a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner has won over this exact course and distance on good ground (1W1P in eight sim-going starts) and Matthew Lloyd Slater takes a 7lb claim; natural hold-up horse who has already demonstrated he can close at Brighton, making him the most credible off-the-pace threat.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and visor in place for Michael Appleby; steps back in trip from seven and eight furlongs to six, and while good-ground form is there (4th twice), zero wins from fifteen similar-going runs suggests a horse who performs consistently but cannot quite win.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's second string but Marco Ghiani takes over and this horse has won at Brighton over 6f on good ground — the only other runner besides Big Time Rascal and Port Hedland with a course victory in similar conditions; 0W1P in limited sim-going runs, but the course-and-distance win stands out.

runners_data.name: Frankali
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying a 7lb claimer (Callan) and wearing blinkers; natural hold-up horse who has been crowded to the rear by the redistribution, and only one run on comparable ground from ten gives very limited evidence — the 3rd on that occasion was his best recent effort.

runners_data.name: Lesley Buckley
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a ⚠ fade flag, suggesting she ties up late — the worst possible profile in a race where hold-up horses need a strong finish; compressed to a midfield map position she wouldn't naturally occupy, and the form string (9-0873) is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Saeculamation
runners_data.note: George Margarson's three-year-old has a solid recent Brighton 6f record (6th, 4th, 3rd, 4th in four good-ground runs) and is the most course-consistent of the redistribution horses; likely to push forward rather than settle deep, and that hidden prominent intent makes him worth tracking if the race falls apart tactically.

races.paceDynamic: Big Time Rascal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and should lead from the gates on good-to-firm ground at Brighton, setting a sustainable gallop that is unlikely to be seriously pressured from behind. The bulk of this field are genuine hold-up horses — Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Valsharah, Manhattan Chute and others — who will need to close from off the pace, while the redistribution flags on Saeculamation, Lynwood Lad, Frankali, Apple's Angel, Battle Point, Coast, Lesley Buckley and Saeculamation confirm the field holds far more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear. Of those redistribution horses, Lynwood Lad (headgear, previous prominent mark) and Saeculamation (consistent good-ground 6f form) are best-placed to push forward and claim a prominent berth if they choose to use the field compression early. With one genuine pace-setter cruising at a comfortable tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or land in a stalking position just off the leader, rather than deep closers who will need a strong end-to-end gallop that simply may not materialise.

watchPoints.text: Big Time Rascal — if Kieren Fox allows any horse to creep within a length on the turn, the leader's energy advantage evaporates quickly on this undulating Brighton straight.

Washington Heir and Port Hedland — both have won over this exact course and distance in similar going, and if either secures a prominent tracking position behind Big Time Rascal they become the primary dangers entering the final furlong.

Lynwood Lad and Saeculamation — these two redistribution horses are the most likely to push forward from their mapped midfield positions early, potentially injecting more pace than the current race shape predicts and tightening up the finish for true hold-up horses.

Manhattan Chute — 54 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field; watch for signs of rustiness in the paddock or early strides, as a hold-up horse returning cold in a steady-run race has very little to work with.

Lesley Buckley — the fade flag combined with a redistribution tag means she carries compounded risk; if she is seen travelling strongly past halfway it may be a false read, as her tendency to stop in the finish is the defining concern.

races.paceDynamic: My Boy Harry is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to challenge for the lead, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating mile. The rest of the field — Rogue Dynasty, Spirit Of Albion, Buy The Dip, Marsh Benham, King Of War and Antiquity — are all natural hold-up horses, meaning My Boy Harry will set every fraction unchallenged and can conserve energy through the middle sections before quickening on the descent to the home straight. Brighton's unique topology rewards horses that can travel into a good position early, since the sharp bend into the straight and the pronounced dip-and-rise finish make it genuinely difficult to make up ground from a cold hold-up berth. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Buy The Dip, Marsh Benham, King Of War and Antiquity are all redistributed forward, meaning at least some must race against their natural instincts or accept a deeply unfavourable position. This race shape unambiguously favours a hold-up horse that can track the pace through the bend and produce a sustained, well-timed run down the hill — not a pure closer coming from last, since the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a fast-finish cavalry charge.

watchPoints.text: My Boy Harry's gallop tempo is the single biggest variable — if Ashley Lewis (5lb) sets an unusually slow pace, all the hold-up horses will be required to make an uncharacteristic early move into the sharp bend or accept a very long run home.

King Of War returns just 8 days after his last run and has his best form over 7f — watch whether J F Egan commits to tracking My Boy Harry from the outset or waits too long, because Brighton leaves little room to make up ground late.

Buy The Dip and Marsh Benham are both true hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map — in a small field of seven, Pat Cosgrave and Jack Callan must decide early whether to push for a stalking position or accept the rear, and traffic through the dip could be decisive.

Marsh Benham's 211-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — George Baker has not had a runner recently and the horse's turf fitness on first return should be monitored in the paddock before drawing conclusions about its market position.

Brighton's sharp cambered bend into the straight means that horses drawn widest or racing without cover into the turn are at a persistent disadvantage — positional decisions in the first three furlongs will be magnified by the course's unusual geography.

races.paceDynamic: Aneirin's Sword is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this five-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to contest the lead, will control fractions entirely on their own terms over Brighton's undulating mile. On Good to Firm ground this shapes as a sustainable, even-tempo lead that will not blow up — the horse can dictate every yard without burning energy fighting for position, which historically suits front-runners at this track. Although Hove Ranger and She's Crafty carry hold-up profiles, both have been redistributed in the map because the field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically sit at the rear in a five-runner race with just one genuine leader; Aneirin's Sword is most likely to secure and maintain the rail position, with the others forced to loom closer than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: a race run at a controlled gallop with a lone, unpressured leader strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile, and hold-up horses who want a strong pace to chase will be at a structural disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Man Is King is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Brighton handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Josephine Gordon can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the front on Good To Firm ground. The remainder of the field — Bohemian Breeze, Annexation, Voix De Bocelli, Cartwheel, San Francisco Bay and Twilight Guest — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Man Is King faces zero genuine pace pressure and can control tempo entirely to suit herself. Little She is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and may attempt to track Man Is King, but she is unlikely to force the issue. This race shape — a lone, unchallenged leader on fast ground over a distance that suits galloping types — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or close from just off the pace, as the hold-up runners will be racing out of their natural role and will face a stiff task generating finishing momentum against a horse allowed to control its own rhythm. Several runners tagged as redistributed (Voix De Bocelli, Cartwheel, San Francisco Bay, Twilight Guest) are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because there is simply no room for all of them at the rear; Man Is King is most likely to secure the front, with Little She best placed to lock onto the leader's quarters.

watchPoints.text: Man Is King's unchallenged lead is the central danger — if Josephine Gordon is allowed to dictate an uncontested gallop, she could be very difficult to catch in the straight and backers of hold-up horses should be forewarned.

Little She is the key tactical tracker — if Ashley Lewis elects to press Man Is King from early on rather than hold a watching brief, she could force the pace higher and change the complexion of the race entirely.

Bohemian Breeze is the most plausible threat from off the pace given her Brighton form, but Tom Queally must judge the pace correctly — if the gallop is too steady her late run may arrive too late on this flat, fast-ground track.

The going report confirms Good To Firm at 1m2f, not merely Good as declared — this fast surface suits front-runners and prominent racers more than hold-up horses, and the several closers in this field should be treated with additional caution.

Voix De Bocelli, Cartwheel, San Francisco Bay and Twilight Guest are all genuine hold-up horses mapping to midfield due to redistribution — none are racing in their natural position, and punters should discount any expectation that they will produce their best form from a mid-pack berth.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Mojito is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Brighton's undulating 7f, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but uncontested gallop with no rival willing or able to press it early. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Prefer The Sister, Lunanova, Henry Tudor, Ridgeway Redwing and Almavillalobas are all genuine closers who have been pushed into midfield on the map simply because there is nowhere else to put them, while Dion Baker, Joycean Way and Jackson Street add further rear-to-midfield weight. This creates a race where the true front plays out at honest but not brutal fractions, and the hold-up brigade will be competing for limited real estate off a single pace-setter who faces no natural pressure. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can race prominently with cover or sit just behind the pace and travel into the race, rather than a true closer who needs a pressured, strung-out gallop to deliver — and it rewards the in-form hold-up type who can make up ground from midfield if the pace is just sufficient. Bear in mind the field holds far more hold-up types than can all secure a genuine late run: of those truly needing cover, Prefer The Sister and Lunanova have the best recent form to mount a challenge, but most will be stuck in traffic fighting for the same ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Them Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses thread through for a late flourish across the wide Brighton straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses thread through for a late flourish across the wide Brighton straight.

watchPoints.text: Dion Baker's hat-trick form (three wins from three at 6-7f Good) makes him the obvious pace threat, but watch whether John Egan can get him into a position close enough to the pace from a hold-up style — if traffic builds behind the field he may arrive too late.

Havana Mojito will attempt to steal this race from the front with no competition for the lead; if Jack Callan (claim, 3lb) allows the mare to slide into an uncontested canter through the first half-mile, the winning margin for the front could be decisive before hold-up horses have got going.

The cluster of five true hold-up types (Prefer The Sister, Lunanova, Henry Tudor, Ridgeway Redwing, Almavillalobas) are all likely to be fighting for the same ground in the straight — a significant traffic risk in the final 2f that could cost the best-performing closer a clear passage.

Starsong has not raced beyond 6f in her recent form string; watch how Harry Davies positions her in the early stages — if she drops back to hold-up territory she is out of role, and if she tracks Havana Mojito she becomes the most interesting prominent threat.

Brighton's 7f is run on a pronounced curve and downhill grade before the straight; horses on the wide outside early often suffer — watch the draw and early positioning for the runners stepping up from 6f (Starsong) or dropping back in class.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 3yo returns after a 155-day absence with a modest recent form string of 452-59, holds a natural hold-up style that suits a race with a strong pace, but 0 wins and 0 places on similar going from 2 runs is a concern, and 155 days off the track adds fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Venetian Romance
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claim) partners this hold-up 3yo who has placed on Good ground (4th, 7f) suggesting the conditions suit, but five consecutive runs without a win and a headgear of 'p' (presumably a previously worn hood) flags a horse that needs everything to fall right for a late challenge.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's runner races just 4 days after its last run which raises freshness questions; a genuine hold-up horse whose true style is placed into midfield on this map because of the overcrowded rear — has placed on Good ground and may push forward to grab a prominent berth given the circumstances.

runners_data.name: Miss Starlet
runners_data.note: George Margarson fields this 3yo who has shown some consistency at 7f on Standard ground (3rd, 4th) but is winless and her natural hold-up style is squeezed by a field full of closers; the race shape, absent a true pace collapse, does not obviously set up for her.

runners_data.name: Pimentel
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's 3yo has the best recent win form in this field (1W, 3P on Good, including a win at 7f on Good going) and is fitted with a 'p' hood; a genuine hold-up type by mapping, but his class edge and good-ground record mean he is the most likely of the redistributed closers to push forward and feature prominently — the style-fit discount is modest given his form advantage.

runners_data.name: Electrocution
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's 3yo arrives on the back of a wide variety of finishes (1,3,3,9,8 recently) and is fitted with a 'b' (blinkers); mapped into midfield from a true hold-up style, and the blinkers change is the key watch here — could sharpen focus and encourage a more forward-going role, but form is inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Pretty Danielle
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race, flagged as a NON-RUNNER for her named jockey which introduces uncertainty over how aggressively she is ridden; has 4 runs at 7f on Standard and one on Good (9th), and despite 0 wins on similar going, the uncontested lead on quick ground makes her the pivotal tactical presence in this race.

races.paceDynamic: Pretty Danielle is the sole confirmed front-runner here, and with the NON-RUNNER flag attached to her jockey this adds a complication to how assertively she is ridden, though she will still likely be sent forward from her natural lead style. With one horse setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Brighton's 7f on Good to Firm ground, the tempo is unlikely to be severe, and that shapes this as a race where the lead could be controlled and untroubled throughout. The field is stacked with hold-up horses — Norcross Brow, Pimentel, Miss Starlet, Electrocution, Venetian Romance and Credit Forgedd It all carry hold-up profiles, meaning five of the seven runners are genuine closers competing for the same ground at the rear, and not all will get their preferred wide, late-running berth. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, with Pimentel and Norcross Brow most likely to push forward and secure a prominent berth given their recent form and positional flexibility. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone front-runner on quick ground with a pack of closers who will block each other out strongly favours the horse who leads or travels prominently close to that uncontested pace.

watchPoints.text: Pretty Danielle's jockey is flagged NON-RUNNER — confirm the replacement rider and whether they will still be instructed to lead, as any change in tactics removes the only confirmed front-runner and fundamentally reshapes this race.

Pimentel and Norcross Brow are both natural hold-up horses who may be forced forward given the overcrowded rear — watch early stall positions and opening strides to see which of the two secures a prominent pitch and which gets blocked behind the pack.

Electrocution's blinkers are a significant headgear change — if they sharpen her jumping-off point she could be more forward than her hold-up tag suggests, adding an unexpected element to the early pace picture.

With five hold-up horses in a seven-runner field, traffic and interference inside the final two furlongs is a material risk — horses that secure a clear outside run early will have a significant advantage over those queuing on the inner.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this 5:15 race, favouring horses with proven quick-ground form; Pimentel's win at 7f on Good stands out in this context and is worth tracking against the pace scenario that unfolds.
